title: Outline & Ring
definition: Utilities for creating focus rings and outlines, essential for accessibility and modern form styling.
simpleExplanation: When you click on an input field, it glows blue. This is called a focus ring. Tailwind's `ring` utility uses CSS box-shadows to create perfectly smooth, customizable glow effects around buttons and inputs that don't mess up your layout dimensions.
realWorldExample: Removing the ugly default browser outline from an input field (`focus:outline-none`) and replacing it with a beautiful branded Tailwind ring (`focus:ring-2 focus:ring-brand-500`).

basic: What is the difference between a `border` and an `outline/ring`?
intermediate: Why is Tailwind's `ring` utility often preferred over standard `outline`?

answers.question: Border vs Outline?
answers.answer: A `border` takes up physical space and pushes other elements away. An `outline` or `ring` is drawn OVER the surrounding elements and takes up zero physical space.

answers.question: Ring vs Outline?
answers.answer: Standard CSS `outline` is historically rigid and hard to style with rounded corners. Tailwind's `ring` is built using box-shadows, which flawlessly follow the exact curve of your `border-radius`.

codeExample:
<!-- The Ultimate Accessible Button -->
<!-- 
  1. focus:outline-none removes the ugly default browser square ring.
  2. focus:ring-2 adds a 2px custom ring.
  3. focus:ring-blue-400 colors it.
  4. focus:ring-offset-2 adds a tiny gap between the button and the ring!
-->
<button class="bg-blue-600 text-white px-4 py-2 rounded-full 
               focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-400 focus:ring-offset-2">
  Click Me
</button>
